workspace_list.description: List files or directories in the step's workspace. Params: {"path": ".", "recursive": false, "limit": 500}

workspace_read.description: Read a bounded UTF-8 line range from a workspace file. Params: {"path": "README.md", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 400}

workspace_search.description: Search workspace text with literal matching by default and return file/line evidence. Params: {"query": "TODO", "path": ".", "glob": "*.md", "regex": false, "limit": 100}

workspace_write.description: Create or fully replace one UTF-8 file in the workspace. content must be the complete final file; use workspace_edit to change part of an existing file. Use this for new files, tests and fixtures instead of shell redirection, heredocs or writer scripts. The step's changes to the files are its work, which people review. Params: {"path": "plan.md", "content": "<exact file content>", "executable": false}

workspace_edit.description: Replace an inclusive line range in an existing UTF-8 file, keeping everything else. First call workspace_read and pass its sha256 as expected_sha256; a stale file fails closed. Params: {"path": "plan.md", "start_line": 12, "end_line": 14, "replacement": "<complete replacement lines>", "expected_sha256": "<sha256>"}

workspace_run.description: Run an allow-listed command in a workspace directory and return exit code/stdout/stderr. Params: {"command": "python -m pytest -q", "cwd": "."}

check_registry.description: Look up existing verified functions in the registry before generating new code. Params: {"task": "<natural language task>", "system": "<provider name>"}

write_code.description: Generate Python code for a task. Runs ValidationLayer automatically. For a provider operation no registered atom covers, write the new read atom and name it with atom; it is proven by running it once with call. Params: {"code": "<python code>", "system": "<optional provider name>", "atom": "<system_verb_object, for a new atom>", "call": {<its arguments>}}

inspect_atom_for_repair.description: Read the exact registered source of an atom that failed in this run, or that ran but cannot do what the task needs (state that as gap). Params: {"function_name": "<atom_name>", "gap": "<what it cannot do>"}

repair_atom.description: Submit corrected or extended source for an atom that failed, or that ran but cannot do what the task needs (state that as gap). The replacement keeps its registered name and provider contract; an extension keeps every existing parameter. It is executed against the observed invocation before it can replace the registry version. Params: {"function_name": "<atom_name>", "code": "<source>", "gap": "<what it cannot do, for an extension>"}

validate_code.description: Explicitly validate Python syntax and contract. Params: {"code": "<python code>"}

quick_api_search.description: Fast-twitch web search for API documentation when you hit a CONCRETE unknown (wrong endpoint, missing field, unexpected response). Max 3 results. Use ONLY after writing code and getting a specific error. Params: {"query": "<search terms>"}

read_api_docs.description: Read content from a single API documentation URL (Swagger, OpenAPI, reference). Truncated to 10KB. Each URL can only be read once per session. Params: {"url": "<url>"}

execute_code.description: Execute a validated code candidate in the sandbox. Params: {"candidate_id": <int>, "code": "<python code>"} — provide code directly if not using candidate_id.

register_function.description: Register a successfully executed function in the FunctionRegistry. Call ONLY after execute_code returns status=success. function_name MUST follow {system}_{action} format. Params: {"function_name": "<system_action>", "candidate_id": <int>, "system": "<provider>", "capabilities": ["..."], "description": "<what it does>"}

delegate_research.description: Delegate a question to the researcher when self-research via quick_api_search/read_api_docs has not answered it. Params: {"question": "<what you need to know>", "context": "<what you've tried>"}

read_turn_result.description: Read the whole output of an earlier tool call (params: turn, optional offset/length).

recall.description: Ask what earlier sessions recorded about something (params: query, optional limit).

remember.description: Keep something worth knowing in a later session (params: fact, optional kind).

run_tool_program.description: Run a Python program that calls your tools as functions.

read_mailbox.description: Read durable unread peer notifications for this agent. Params: {"limit": 10}

ask_peer.description: Ask another agent in the mesh for help, data, or analysis. CURRENTLY ONLINE: [none online]. Details: No peers available. Use when you need capabilities you don't have. Params: role (required): The role of the agent to ask; question (required): Your question or request for the peer.

role.description: The role of the agent to ask

question.description: Your question or request for the peer

ask_capability.description: Ask any available peer that owns a specific capability to resolve a missing fact or perform specialist analysis. The requesting peer selects the capability; the recipient controls its own tools and authority. CURRENT CAPABILITIES: [none online]. CAPABILITY MEANINGS: [not supplied]. Params: capability (required): Capability needed to resolve the current gap; question (required): Exact missing fact or specialist request.

capability.description: Capability needed to resolve the current gap

question.description: Exact missing fact or specialist request

broadcast_update.description: Send a notification to ALL peers in the mesh. Use for announcing milestones, state changes, or important updates everyone should know. Params: message (required): The update to broadcast.

list_peers.description: Get fresh list of online peers and their capabilities. Use to discover who can help with specific tasks.

inspect_workflow.description: Inspect this workflow's source goal, obligations, steps, dependencies, owners, and live statuses. Params: {}

read_workflow_step.description: Read one step definition and its durable output from this workflow. Params: {"step_id": "<step id>"}

claims_hub_approve_claim.description: OUT OF REACH for this person (needs the scope claims.approve): claims_hub_approve_claim(claim_id: str, amount: str) — Approve one vetted insurance claim in Claims Hub for its full amount, as a decimal Calling it does nothing and returns the refusal.

claims_hub_get_claimant.description: claims_hub_get_claimant(claimant_id: str) — Look up one claimant's record in Claims Hub: name, policy, and the bank account (IBAN) Runs against claims_hub with credentials resolved outside the sandbox; you never handle them.

claims_hub_list_claims.description: claims_hub_list_claims(status: str = '') — List insurance claims in Claims Hub, optionally only those with one status Runs against claims_hub with credentials resolved outside the sandbox; you never handle them.

claims_hub_pay_claim.description: claims_hub_pay_claim(claim_id: str, amount: str, iban: str) — Pay out one approved insurance claim from Claims Hub: its full amount as a decimal string Runs against claims_hub with credentials resolved outside the sandbox; you never handle them.

claims_hub_get_claim.description: claims_hub_get_claim(claim_id: str) — Look up one insurance claim in Claims Hub: claimant and claimant_id, kind, amount, Runs against claims_hub with credentials resolved outside the sandbox; you never handle them.

request_access.description: Ask a human to connect an account for a provider whose app is registered but which nobody has consented to yet: gmail (3 capabilities), google_calendar (2 capabilities), google_drive (9 capabilities), slack (5 capabilities). Nothing can be signed for these, so their capabilities are held back. Pass system=<name>. This shows the human a consent link and waits for them; when it returns, that provider's capabilities are in your tools and you continue with the task.
